title: Paris Saint-Germain 2-2 Roma: Malen penalty ends champions' perfect start
subtitle: FotMob
paragraphs: NewsAboutParis Saint-Germain 2-2 Roma: Malen penalty ends champions' perfect startShareRoma were the first side to avoid defeat against Paris Saint-Germain in this season's Champions League after penalty drama in Paris.Paris Saint-Germain's perfect Champions League run came to an end as Donyell Malen's penalty snatched a 2-2 draw for Roma at the Parc des Princes.

The defending European champions were the only side to win their first four games in the league phase, but a fifth straight victory went amiss after Malen's spot-kick 12 minutes from time on Wednesday.

Mario Hermoso earlier silenced the home crowd when slamming in a fifth-minute opener from close range after winning possession high up the pitch, before finishing with aplomb following Matias Soule's cutback pass.
However, poor Roma defending from Senny Mayulu's right-sided corner allowed Illia Zabarnyi to head in a near-post leveller for his first Champions League goal just past the half-hour mark.
Nuno Mendes saw another low drive repelled by Mile Svilar, while Evan Ndicka passed up a great headed opportunity from Roma's corner on the stroke of half-time at the other end.
Hermoso volleyed narrowly over immediately after the interval from Wesley's outside-of-the-boot cross, before Matvey Safonov expertly denied Niccolo Pisilli.
PSG went close when Joao Neves headed just wide of the bottom-left corner before Achraf Hakimi broke in behind and won a penalty for Wesley's clumsy tug on the right-back's shirt.
Substitute Ousmane Dembele duly converted from 12 yards, sliding into the bottom-right corner in the 62nd minute, to spark rapturous celebrations from the home supporters.
But Roma hit back with a penalty of their own after VAR deemed Vitinha to have handled Soule's close-range effort, with Malen sweeping into the left of the net to equalise.
Hermoso then squandered another opportunity late on, while Svilar stood firm against Dembele as PSG were somewhat fortunate to escape with a point.
Roma frustration turns to celebration through Malen
Heading into the fifth matchday, Roma had been in losing positions for just 4% of their Champions League games – the lowest percentage of any side this season.
However, through those first four games, Roma also dropped more points from winning positions (eight) than any other team.
That pattern followed clearly here, as Hermoso's well-taken opener was swiftly cancelled out by Roma's slack set-piece defending for a simple Zabarnyi header.

Gian Piero Gasperini could be seen fuming on the touchline after Roma's corner concession led to an avoidable equaliser, but his side still only allowed PSG chances worth a meagre 0.4 expected goals (xG) in the first half.
Another lapse in concentration proved Roma's undoing after the interval, with Wesley somewhat fortunate to escape a red card after dragging down Hakimi for Dembele's penalty.
But the ever-reliable Malen stepped up once again in Gasperini's time of need.

He has now been directly involved in seven goals in the Champions League this season (five goals, two assists). The only Roma player with more goal involvements in a single edition is Edin Dzeko (10 in 2017-18 and eight in 2018-19), and Malen could soon chase that record down.

Gasperini will feel this was a deserved point, at the very least, after Roma accumulated 2.69 xG to PSG's 1.78 total in Paris as Luis Enrique's side saw a run of 12 straight wins in all competitions come to an end.
